Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Discontent among the Khorasani Arabs rose sharply after the losses suffered in the Battle of the Defile in 731.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: In 734, al-_____ ibn Surayj led a revolt that received broad backing from Arab settlers and native inhabitants alike, capturing Balkh but failing to take Merv
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: In 734, al-Harith ibn Surayj led a revolt that received broad backing from Arab settlers and native inhabitants alike, capturing Balkh but failing to take Merv. After this defeat, al-Harith's movement seems to have been dissolved.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: In 744, Yazid III, a son of al-Walid I, was proclaimed caliph in _____, while his army killed al-Walid II
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: In 744, Yazid III, a son of al-Walid I, was proclaimed caliph in Damascus, while his army killed al-Walid II. Yazid had appointed his brother, Ibrahim, as his successor, but Marwan II (744–750), the grandson of Marwan I, led an army from the northern frontier and entered Damascus in December 744, where he was proclaimed caliph.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Marwan immediately moved the capital north to _____, in present-day Turkey
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Marwan immediately moved the capital north to Harran, in present-day Turkey.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: A rebellion soon broke out in Syria, perhaps due to resentment over the relocation of the capital, and in 746 Marwan razed the walls of Homs and _____ in retaliation
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Yazid had appointed his brother, Ibrahim, as his successor, but Marwan II (744–750), the grandson of Marwan I, led an army from the northern frontier and entered Damascus in December 744, where he was proclaimed caliph. Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Marwan also faced significant opposition from _____ in Iraq and Iran, who put forth first Dahhak ibn Qays and then Abu Dulaf as rival caliphs
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Marwan also faced significant opposition from Kharijites in Iraq and Iran, who put forth first Dahhak ibn Qays and then Abu Dulaf as rival caliphs.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: In 747, _____ managed to reestablish control of Iraq, but by this time a more serious threat had arisen in Khorasan
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Marwan immediately moved the capital north to Harran, in present-day Turkey. A rebellion soon broke out in Syria, perhaps due to resentment over the relocation of the capital, and in 746 Marwan razed the walls of Homs and Damascus in retaliation.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The Abbasids were members of the _____ clan, rivals of the Umayyads, but the word "Hashimiyya" seems to refer specifically to Abu Hashim, a grandson of Ali and son of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: According to certain traditions, _____ died in 717 in Humayma in the house of Muhammad ibn Ali, the head of the Abbasid family, and before dying named Muhammad ibn Ali as his successor
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: The Abbasids were members of the Banu Hashim clan, rivals of the Umayyads, but the word "Hashimiyya" seems to refer specifically to Abu Hashim, a grandson of Ali and son of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya. According to certain traditions, Abu Hashim died in 717 in Humayma in the house of Muhammad ibn Ali, the head of the Abbasid family, and before dying named Muhammad ibn Ali as his successor.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: This tradition allowed the _____ to rally the supporters of the failed revolt of Mukhtar al-Thaqafi, who had represented themselves as the supporters of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: The Abbasids were members of the Banu Hashim clan, rivals of the Umayyads, but the word "Hashimiyya" seems to refer specifically to Abu Hashim, a grandson of Ali and son of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya. This tradition allowed the Abbasids to rally the supporters of the failed revolt of Mukhtar al-Thaqafi, who had represented themselves as the supporters of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya.

Umayyad Caliphate.question: Beginning around 719, _____ missions began to seek adherents in Khurasan
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: The Abbasids were members of the Banu Hashim clan, rivals of the Umayyads, but the word "Hashimiyya" seems to refer specifically to Abu Hashim, a grandson of Ali and son of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya. Beginning around 719, Hashimiyya missions began to seek adherents in Khurasan.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: They sought support for a "member of the family" of _____, without making explicit mention of the Abbasids
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: This tradition allowed the Abbasids to rally the supporters of the failed revolt of Mukhtar al-Thaqafi, who had represented themselves as the supporters of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya. Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Umayyad Caliphate.fact: These missions met with success both among Arabs and non-Arabs (mawali), although the latter may have played a particularly important role in the growth of the movement.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Around 746, _____ assumed leadership of the Hashimiyya in Khurasan
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Around 746, Abu Muslim assumed leadership of the Hashimiyya in Khurasan.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: He soon established control of _____, expelling its Umayyad governor, Nasr ibn Sayyar, and dispatched an army westwards
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Around 746, Abu Muslim assumed leadership of the Hashimiyya in Khurasan. He soon set up control of Khurasan, expelling its Umayyad governor, Nasr ibn Sayyar, and dispatched an army westwards.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: At this point _____ mobilized his troops from Harran and advanced toward Iraq
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: At this point Marwan mobilized his troops from Harran and advanced toward Iraq. Damascus fell to the Abbasids in April, and in August, Marwan was killed in Egypt.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: In January 750 the two forces met in the Battle of the Zab, and the _____ were defeated
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: In January 750 the two forces met in the Battle of the Zab, and the Umayyads were defeated. Some Umayyads in Syria continued to resist the takeover.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Damascus fell to the _____ in April, and in August, Marwan was killed in Egypt
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Damascus fell to the Abbasids in April, and in August, Marwan was killed in Egypt.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Some Umayyads in _____ continued to resist the takeover
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Some Umayyads in Syria continued to resist the takeover. The Umayyad princes Abu Muhammad al-Sufyani, al-Abbas ibn Muhammad, and Hashim ibn Yazid launched revolts in Syria and the Islamic–Byzantine frontier around late 750, but they were defeated.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The Umayyad princes _____ al-Sufyani, al-Abbas ibn Muhammad, and Hashim ibn Yazid launched revolts in Syria and the Islamic–Byzantine frontier around late 750, but they were defeated

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The victors desecrated the tombs of the _____ in Syria, sparing only that of Umar II, and most of the remaining members of the Umayyad family were tracked down and killed
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Some Umayyads in Syria continued to resist the takeover. The victors desecrated the tombs of the Umayyads in Syria, sparing only that of Umar II, and most of the remaining members of the Umayyad family were tracked down and killed.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: One grandson of _____, Abd al-Rahman I, survived, escaped across North Africa, and established an emirate in Moorish Iberia (Al-Andalus)
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: One grandson of Hisham, Abd al-Rahman I, survived, escaped across North Africa, and set up an emirate in Moorish Iberia (Al-Andalus).

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Some Umayyads also survived in Syria, and their descendants would once more attempt to restore their old regime during the _____
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Some Umayyads also survived in Syria, and their descendants would once more attempt to restore their old regime during the Fourth Fitna.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Two Umayyads, Abu al-_____ al-Sufyani and Maslama ibn Ya'qub, successively seized control of Damascus from 811 to 813, and declared themselves caliphs
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Two Umayyads, Abu al-Umaytir al-Sufyani and Maslama ibn Ya'qub, successively seized control of Damascus from 811 to 813, and declared themselves caliphs.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: During the Umayyad period, mass conversions brought _____, Berbers, Copts, and Aramaic to Islam
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: During the Umayyad period, mass conversions brought Persians, Berbers, Copts, and Aramaic to Islam.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: These mawalis (clients) were often better educated and more civilised than their _____ overlords
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: These mawalis (clients) were often better educated and more civilised than their Arab overlords.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The new converts, on the basis of equality of all _____, transformed the political landscape

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

As the central power of the Umayyad rulers waned in the later years of the dynasty, some governors neglected to send the extra tax revenue to Damascus and created great personal fortunes.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: These were supported by tribes in the Syrian desert and in the frontier with the Byzantines, as well as _____ tribes

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Soldiers were registered with the _____, the Diwan Al-Jaysh, and were salaried
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Soldiers were registered with the Army Ministry, the Diwan Al-Jaysh, and were salaried.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: There were likely around 300,000 troops enrolled in the registers in 700, though _____ gives the larger figure of 400,000 for the reign of Hisham
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: There were likely around 300,000 troops enrolled in the registers in 700, though Blankinship gives the larger figure of 400,000 for the reign of Hisham.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Before Iraq was demilitarised in wake of the 701 revolt of Ibn al-Ash'ath, it had over 100,000 troops on its _____ (Basra - 80,000; Kufa - 60,000)
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Before Iraq was demilitarised in wake of the 701 revolt of Ibn al-Ash'ath, it had over 100,000 troops on its Diwan (Basra - 80,000; Kufa - 60,000).

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Adjusting for the potential unreliability of these reports, a total force of 250,000-300,000 is a reasonable estimate, consistent with the army sizes of the _____ and Sasanian empires
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Adjusting for the potential unreliability of these reports, a total force of 250,000-300,000 is a reasonable estimate, consistent with the army sizes of the Late Roman and Sasanian empires.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The Umayyad Syrian forces specialized in close order infantry warfare and favored using a kneeling spear wall formation in battle, probably as a result of their encounters with _____ armies

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: This was radically different from the original _____ style of mobile and individualistic fighting
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: This was radically different from the original Bedouin style of mobile and individualistic fighting.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: In addition to this, the Umayyad government began to mint its own coins in _____, which were initially similar to pre-existing coins but evolved in an independent direction
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: In addition to this, the Umayyad government began to mint its own coins in Damascus, which were initially similar to pre-existing coins but evolved in an independent direction.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: These were the first coins minted by a _____ government in history
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: These were the first coins minted by a Muslim government in history.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Early _____ coins re-used Byzantine and Sasanian iconography directly but added new Islamic elements
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Early Islamic coins re-used Byzantine and Sasanian iconography directly but added new Islamic elements. On the reverse side, the traditional Byzantine cross-on-steps image was modified to avoid any explicitly non-Islamic connotation.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Early Islamic coins re-used Byzantine and Sasanian iconography directly but added new Islamic elements. So-called "Arab-Byzantine" coins replicated Byzantine coins and were minted in Levantine cities before and after the Umayyads rose to power.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: On the reverse side, the traditional _____ cross-on-steps image was modified to avoid any explicitly non-Islamic connotation
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Early Islamic coins re-used Byzantine and Sasanian iconography directly but added new Islamic elements. So-called "Arab-Byzantine" coins replicated Byzantine coins and were minted in Levantine cities before and after the Umayyads rose to power.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Some examples of these coins, likely minted in _____, copied the coins of Byzantine emperor Heraclius, including a depiction of the emperor and his son Heraclius Constantine
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Some examples of these coins, likely minted in Damascus, copied the coins of Byzantine emperor Heraclius, including a depiction of the emperor and his son Heraclius Constantine.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: In the 690s, under Abd al-_____'s reign, a new period of experimentations began

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: This was possibly an attempt to depict the act of _____ prayer or the delivery of the khutba (Friday sermon)
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: This was possibly an attempt to depict the act of Muslim prayer or the delivery of the khutba (Friday sermon).

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The spear is believed to be the spear ('anaza) that _____ carried before him when entering the mosque
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: The spear is believed to be the spear ('anaza) that Muhammad carried before him when entering the mosque.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The coins generally featured _____ inscriptions without any images, ending the earlier iconographic traditions

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The main gold unit was the dinar (from _____ denarius), which was worth 20 silver coins
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: The main gold unit was the dinar (from Roman denarius), which was worth 20 silver coins.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: It was most likely modeled on the _____ solidus

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Umayyad Caliphate.fact: It was most likely modeled on the Byzantine solidus. Its size and shape was based on Sasanian coins and they were minted in much larger quantities than in the earlier Byzantine era.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The silver coin was called a dirham (from _____ drachma)
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: The silver coin was called a dirham (from Greek drachma).

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Its size and shape was based on _____ coins and they were minted in much larger quantities than in the earlier Byzantine era
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Its size and shape was based on Sasanian coins and they were minted in much larger quantities than in the earlier Byzantine era.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: These images may have been based on _____ representations of the menorah or on earlier Hasmonean models

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The switch to a five-branched version may have been intended to further differentiate this depiction from Jewish and _____ versions
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: These images may have been based on Christian representations of the menorah or on earlier Hasmonean models. The switch to a five-branched version may have been intended to further differentiate this depiction from Jewish and Christian versions.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: The Arab _____ held themselves in higher esteem than Muslim non-Arabs and generally did not mix with other Muslims
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: The Arab Muslims held themselves in higher esteem than Muslim non-Arabs and generally did not mix with other Muslims. As conversions increased, tax revenues from non-Muslims also decreased to dangerous lows.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: As conversions increased, tax revenues from non-_____ also decreased to dangerous lows
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: The Arab Muslims held themselves in higher esteem than Muslim non-Arabs and generally did not mix with other Muslims. As conversions increased, tax revenues from non-Muslims also decreased to dangerous lows.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: As Islam spread, more and more of the _____ population consisted of non-Arabs

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: This caused social unrest, as the new converts were not given the same rights as _____
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: This caused social unrest, as the new converts were not given the same rights as Muslim Arabs.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: These issues continued to worsen until they helped cause the _____ revolution in the 740s
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: These issues continued to worsen until they helped cause the Abbasid revolution in the 740s.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: They were given a legally protected status as second-class citizens as long as they accepted and acknowledged the political supremacy of the ruling _____
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: As conversions increased, tax revenues from non-Muslims also decreased to dangerous lows. They were given a legally protected status as second-class citizens as long as they accepted and acknowledged the political supremacy of the ruling Muslims.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: More specifically, non-_____ had to pay a tax, known as jizya, which the Muslims did not have to pay; Muslims would instead pay the zakat tax
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: As conversions increased, tax revenues from non-Muslims also decreased to dangerous lows. They were given a legally protected status as second-class citizens as long as they accepted and acknowledged the political supremacy of the ruling Muslims.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: If non-_____ converted to Islam, they would cease paying jizya and would instead pay zakat
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: They were given a legally protected status as second-class citizens as long as they accepted and acknowledged the political supremacy of the ruling Muslims. Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Although the _____ were harsh when it came to defeating their Zoroastrian adversaries, they did offer protection and relative religious tolerance to the Zoroastrians who accepted their authority
Umayyad Caliphate.fact: Although the Umayyads were harsh when it came to defeating their Zoroastrian adversaries, they did offer protection and relative religious tolerance to the Zoroastrians who accepted their authority.

Umayyad Caliphate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Umayyad Caliphate.question: Fred Donner says that _____ in the northern parts of Iran were hardly penetrated by the "believers", winning virtually complete autonomy in-return for tribute-tax or jizya

Wedding reception.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Wedding reception.question: A whole fish, chicken, or pig means luck and completeness in _____ wedding culture
Wedding reception.fact: A whole fish, chicken, or pig means luck and completeness in Chinese wedding culture. Very often, the bride will change into a traditional Chinese red wedding dress (鳳褂, or qípáo) at that time, if she has been wearing a different style of clothing before.
